It is newer than every overhead view: its position (about 0.5 m), size and heights are measured in the photograph taken from the court, where its south wall and door end are both in view, with the bay width taken as 2 ft; it stands a few degrees off the compass, parallel to the garden cage. The panels are frosted: the walls only hint at the timber frame inside, and the roof reads as a solid pale blue-grey sheet between white battens, as in all three photographs. Its place along the arbor row comes from two photographs that show both: beside its north-west corner (the gable stands nearer the lens than the first placing gave) and from the door end (the arbor post seen past its south-west corner): about 0.3 m north of the first placing, on the same line of sight from the court.
greenhouse_walls_greenhouse_panel.source: owner's photographs of the greenhouse and of the garden, and the photograph of the garden from the court

about.heading: How this model was made
intro: This is the house and grounds as they stand today, after the 2023 renovation. The appearance - cladding, stone, windows and doors, porches, decks, the outbuildings - follows the owner's own photographs and main-floor plan, checked side by side against renders from the same viewpoints.

Underneath, the geometry is measured rather than drawn by eye: the ground, the tree canopy and the roof planes that predate the renovation come from an airborne laser survey, wall positions from the county's dimensioned record card and the floor plan, and the parcel from county GIS. Switch the display to Evidence and click any part to see what it rests on.
accuracy: Roofs of the house that predate the renovation: 432 laser returns hit them in the 2017 survey; 100% lie within 15 cm of the modelled surface and 100% within 30 cm (median offset -0 cm).
Roofs of the detached garage that predate the renovation: 182 laser returns hit them in the 2017 survey; 100% lie within 15 cm of the modelled surface and 100% within 30 cm (median offset -0 cm).

Parts built or altered in the 2023 renovation, and the pole barn, greenhouse and garden, were fitted to the owner's photographs: each photograph was matched with a camera placed where it was taken, and corners, roof peaks, doors and windows were adjusted until they landed within a few pixels - typically 5 to 20 cm on the building.
The pole barn's position comes from three independent measurements (two photogrammetric solutions and a 2025 overhead view) that agree to within about 25 cm.
Terrain is the 2017 survey's ground surface on a 1 m grid; where the ground has since been regraded (walk-out patio, barn pad) it is levelled to heights read from the photographs.

limits: The model shows the property as the owner's most recent photographs have it. Things that change with the seasons are fixed in one state: the lawn is drawn green, the flower planter in summer growth, and the trees in leaf unless the sun study is set to a winter date.

Trees: most positions and heights come from a 2017 laser survey flown with the leaves off, which finds the dominant crowns and little else. The woods were thickened where that survey saw woody growth, and stands that have grown up since were added from the photographs; stems there are indicative, not located. Crowns and shrubs are stylised.
Walls that no photograph shows are drawn plain and marked as inferred - chiefly the pole barn's south and west walls and the west face of the link between the house and the attached garage.
Small fittings are simplified or left out: lanterns, gutters and downspouts are schematic, and furniture, grills, hoses, vehicles, pots and individual plants are not modelled.
Ground reshaped since the 2017 survey (the walk-out patio, the barn pad, the garden) is levelled to heights read from photographs, good to about 10 to 20 cm.
Doors and windows on walls photographed only at a glancing angle are placed to about 20 to 50 cm along the wall; those photographed square-on to about 5 to 10 cm.
Colours were matched against photographs taken in different light and seasons; a single colour per material cannot match all of them.
Exterior only. The parcel line is the county GIS line and is not a legal boundary.
